title: Halting simulation of a deterministic instruction
statement: Let $m,d,k_D$ be nonnegative integers, let $\Lambda$ and $SD$ be state sets, and fix a Boolean input $x$, an augmented register machine $A$ with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, an initial label $l_0$, an oracle, a $k_D$-work-tape Turing machine $D$, initial decider states $q_0$, bounds $B,W,P$, a label $l$, register contents $v$, a Boolean memory tape $M$ with head position $p$, an output word $out$, and a bit $b_0$. Suppose the instruction at $l$ is the deterministic instruction $i$, and the ordinary register-machine execution from $(l,v)$ with no prior answer halts with unchanged registers $v$ and answer $b_0$. Suppose also that the stated precondition holds at this configuration, every register satisfies $|\mathrm{bits}(v(r)+1)|\le W$, and $|p|\le P$. Then the compiled Turing machine, started with input $x$, register contents $v$, memory tape $M$ at position $p$, and output $out$, reaches a halting configuration whose output is $out$ followed by $b_0$, and every configuration up to that time satisfies the register, decider-work-tape, and memory-head bounds $W,B,P$ encoded by $\mathrm{MBox}$.
hypotheses_covered: A is an augmented register machine with m registers and d deciders
l₀ is the compiled machine's initial label
oracle maps each decider and Boolean word to a Boolean answer
D is a k_D-work-tape Boolean Turing machine
q₀ assigns an initial state to each decider
B, W, P are natural-number bounds
l is a program label and A(l) is the deterministic instruction i
v assigns a natural-number value to each register
M is a Boolean-valued memory tape and p is its integer head position
out is the initial output word and b₀ is a Boolean answer
the abstract execution from (l,v) with no answer halts with registers v and answer b₀
the precondition Pre holds at (l,v) with no answer
each register's v(r)+1 binary representation has length at most W
the absolute value of p is at most P
caveat: The auxiliary notions Pre and MBox are supplied only as Lean definitions; the statement describes their roles but their detailed conjunctions are not expanded.
